name: Arizona Biltmore Resort and Spa
positioning: Frank Lloyd Wright-influenced resort on 39 acres of desert gardens in Phoenix, a landmark since 1929, now officially Arizona Biltmore, LXR Hotels & Resorts
best_for: Architecture lovers drawn to Frank Lloyd Wright's design legacy
Families who want a pool with a splash pad, waterslide and swim-up bar
Couples who want an adults-only pool and a desert-inspired spa
Golfers and tennis or pickleball players

facts.text: The resort's architecture is influenced by Frank Lloyd Wright, and it has been a Phoenix landmark since 1929.
The grounds cover 39 acres of desert gardens and reflect the design legacy of Frank Lloyd Wright and his protege Albert Chase McArthur.
Guests can explore the grounds' geometric patterns and signature Biltmore Blocks on an architectural walk.
The resort has seven swimming pools.
Saguaro Pool is reserved for adults.
Tierra Luna Spa's treatments and rituals center on desert botanicals, cosmic connection and dynamic recovery.
Renata's Hearth hosts Latin evenings centered on fire and flavor.
McArthur's Restaurant & Bar, formerly Frank & Albert's, serves New American food.
Cup & Cone is an art deco inspired cafe with espresso, homemade gelato and desserts.
Guests have access to two championship golf courses.
The resort has tennis and pickleball courts, with Har-Tru tennis courts and coaching from PBI coaches.

highlights.text: Catalina Pool is a resort landmark where famous guests, from Marilyn Monroe to Frank Sinatra, have gathered.
Wrigley Mansion, a historic hilltop destination with Christopher's, Geordie's Restaurant and Jamie's Wine Bar, is now part of the Arizona Biltmore experience.
Saguaro Pool is home to a 140-year-old cactus named Lloyd.
Access to the spa's outdoor Sol Garden is included with any 50-minute treatment at Tierra Luna Spa.
Paradise Pool, aimed at families, has a splash pad, a triple 65-foot waterslide and a swim-up bar.

considerations.text: Room rates include a mandatory charge of 59 US dollars per night.
WhataHotel notes that the large resort property requires walking between facilities.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
